To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
blood tests are not a useful tool for the diagnosis of liver disease, and the use of blood tests for this purpose should be discouraged.
the use of blood tests to assess liver function is not recommended in the diagnosis of patients with liver disease, because they are inaccurate, unreliable, and not specific enough.
the liver plays an important role in the metabolism of drugs and other substances in the body.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the liver in health and disease, with particular reference to the use of blood studies in the diagnosis of liver diseases.
the study of the blood in diseases of the liver, with particular attention to the blood picture and the blood chemistry.
the evaluation of the blood studies in diagnosis and prognosis of the liver diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the case of the blood studies, as in the case of all other diagnostic procedures, the physician is the most important factor.
the liver function tests are not specific enough for diagnosis of the various liver diseases.
in a case of liver injury, the blood studies, when properly correlated with the history and physical findings, are of great value in diagnosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found the following tests to be the most useful in the diagnosis of diseases of this organ: 1) the total blood count, especially the differential leukocyte count; 2) the blood sedimentation rate, which is especially useful in acute and subacute diseases; 3) the blood sugar determination, especially in acute diseases; 4) the serum bilirubin, which is of value in the diagnosis of obstructive jaundice, but not of much value in acute diseases;

the following blood studies were found to be of value in the diagnosis of diseases of liver:  (a) The blood urea nitrogen (BUN) test, (b) the alkaline phosphatase test, (c) the total serum bilirubin test, (d) the serum glutamic oxalacetic transaminase (SGOT) test, (e) the total serum protein test, (f) the serum albumin test, (g) the serum globulin
we have found that in the presence of liver disease, the blood studies of the liver are of little value in diagnosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of room for improvement in the current methods of diagnosing and treating liver diseases.
we have shown that it is possible to use a deep neural network to predict the presence of disease from blood samples.
the liver is a complex organ that performs many different functions.
